title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a06_seizure

lines.sfx: Two SUVs and a county flatbed grind up the dirt drive toward the barn.
In the lead SUV a phone runs on speaker in the dashboard mount, the voice on it tinny and close.
The man in the passenger seat is Administrator Pell, fifties, a lanyard he keeps touching.

lines.text: I need one on the books by Saturday, Pell. A real one, serial number and all. You miss it, they fold your office into Lincoln and I quit taking your calls.

lines.sfx: The phone taps dark and the visor snaps down. For a second there's nothing.
The SUV door opens and Pell steps out onto the dirt.
The movers drop the flatbed ramp and a steel dolly rolls off it onto the dirt.
At the barn door Cricket stands with his boots set on the boards and doesn't come out to meet them.
Back in the barn behind him the floor creaks under three men who stay on their feet, Dutch and Stitch and Gunny.

lines.text: (warm) Mr. Dawes. Morning. And thank you, real sincerely, for your patience with all this.

lines.sfx: Cricket doesn't answer.

lines.text: They built these to last, didn't they. You'd pay a fortune for joinery like this over on the continent.

lines.sfx: Pell clicks his pen and runs it down the clipboard.
Pell's pen scratches the correction in.
A mover peels a sticker and presses it flat onto the panel.

lines.text: It was surplus. Nineteen seventy-five. Told it'd be scrapped otherwise.

lines.sfx: A mover cuts across the farmhouse porch and his boots knock over the fresh-painted boards.
Pell slides a notebook off the back shelf and fans the pages.
He turns a page and drops the notebook back crooked on the shelf.
Down at the cradle a wrench works a bolt loose, and the mover on it hisses and shakes his hand.
Cricket lifts a socket off the pegboard and holds it out, and the man takes it without a word.

lines.text: (quiet and hard) Not one of you ever built a thing out here. Now it's all yours.

lines.sfx: Pell's pen stops.

lines.text: You didn't build this either, Mr. Dawes. Nineteen seventy-five it should've gone back to NASA, and it never did, and for fifty years nobody so much as asked. You just had it a long time. Long enough it started to feel like yours.

lines.sfx: Cricket doesn't answer him.
The dolly rolls toward the door with the crew couch strapped down on it.
Cricket steps into the doorway and plants his boots square on the boards.
The dolly stops. Nobody moves.
Wade Halversen, the county deputy, comes across the yard slow with his hat in his hand.

lines.text: You'll have to move me, Wade.
(low) Earl. Federal list came down Tuesday. County don't see a dime off any of it. Nobody does.

lines.sfx: Behind Cricket, Stitch shifts a half step and a board creaks.

lines.text: (to Stitch) Warehouse outside Lincoln, is what I hear. Same one as the rest of it.
(to Cricket) There's a window to appeal it. It's open till four.

lines.sfx: Wade takes Cricket's arm in both hands, and the sleeve cloth bunches under them.
He walks Cricket three steps to the side, and Cricket lets him.
The dolly rolls past the two of them, out the door, and down the ramp.
Pell tucks the clipboard under his arm and turns to the men left in the yard.

lines.text: Folks, I know change feels sudden. But as the Accord reminds us — harmony is a verb.

lines.sfx: Pell gets in the SUV. The trucks and the flatbed pull down the drive, and the engines fade off until the yard goes quiet.
Cricket's boots cross the concrete and stop where the trainer stood, and the empty barn throws the sound back at him.
He lets out one long breath.
He reaches over the workbench and clicks on an old two-way radio the movers never listed, and it comes up in a low hiss.
Dutch, Stitch, and Gunny come in from the yard and stand along the edge of the bare floor with him.
Cricket reaches up and the work light's pull-chain clicks.
